attempted_claim: For every k in S (about 196 sixth-power-free values in (10^7,10^7+200]), a complete certified list L_k = E_k(Z) (both signs of y, including torsion integral points, excluding infinity), with rank r_k and saturated independent generators G_k (ellsaturation, analytic-rank/BSD cross-check where 2-descent leaves an interval), canonical-height vector h_hat on L_k and regulator where r_k>0, and proof of completeness via David lower bounds for linear forms in elliptic logarithms plus LLL reduction (Cremona-de Weger-Smart elliptic-log sieve as implemented in Sage E.integral_points() / PARI ellintegralpoint). Deliver full substitution-checkable point lists, height/Hall-ratio tables, the global maximal-height witness (k*,x*,y*,h_hat*) and maximal Hall-ratio witness, and deterministic scripts/logs so any auditor reruns substitution in seconds and the sieve in minutes-to-hours per curve.
claim_type: complete integral-point census for a bounded coefficient stratum with extremal-height witness
decisive_failure: value: Even though correct and narrowly new, the proved result as stated is not independently worth finding later under SCOPE value gates (textbook restatement / mere parameter substitution / unexplained enumeration). Lane target required Siegel-complete census via David/LLL elliptic-log sieve with rank intervals, saturated generators, Cremona heights/regulators, and global height/Hall witnesses; topic fallback required >=90% Siegel-certified plus explicit bounds/obstructions for remainder. Achieved: 0% Siegel-certified. What remains is: (i) trivial S enumeration by trial division; (ii) torsion triviality which is textbook Fueter/Mazur + square/cube interval check (Lutz divisor check is standard exercise); (iii) exhaustive brute-force table up to arbitrary cutoff B=1e6 (XMIN=-1000) with 23/196 curves nonempty, 173 empty up to B but explicitly possibly nonempty beyond B; Pasten |k|^{1/2+eps} log-bound cited in DRAFT implies true integral points can have x astronomically larger than 1e6, so table is provably a lower-bound fragment, not a census; (iv) rank>=1 trivial corollary of (ii)+(iii); (v) Hall maximizer and naive log heights only among found points (x<=B), not global, with explicit warning not to interpret naive logs as canonical heights — the very canonical-height/regulator artifacts that would make beyond-threshold data citable for rank/regulator/Hall benchmarks (Elkies, D'Mello gaps) are absent. Crossing the 1e7 completeness threshold confers no value without completeness proof: bounded enumeration could be done for any interval, threshold is irrelevant to an incomplete table. Hall max depending on arbitrary B is a property of the search window, not of the curves. Future work needing complete L_k, regulators, or global extrema cannot cite this fragment; it would need to redo the sieve. This is exactly 'unexplained enumeration even if correct and new' and 'mere parameter substitution (next 200 k with arbitrary B)' that the audit brief requires rejecting. No REPAIRABLE fix within presentation exists; completing the sieve/canonical heights is new research, not a fix.

method_summary: canonical-height descent with elliptic-logarithm sieve and exact integral-point substitution verification
problem_statement: Let S = {k in Z : 10^7 < k <= 10^7+200, v_p(k) <= 5 for all primes p} (sixth-power-free, quasi-minimal). For each k in S let E_k/Q : y^2 = x^3 + k (integral model y^2 = x^3 + 0*x + k, discriminant -432*k^2). Determine with certificate the complete affine integral set E_k(Z) = {(x,y) in Z^2 : y^2 = x^3 + k}, together with Mordell-Weil rank r_k, saturated generators G_k, Neron-Tate canonical heights h_hat(P) in Cremona/PARI normalization (Silverman normalization divided by 2), and Hall ratio R(P)=sqrt(|x|)/|k| for x != 0. Identify the global extremal witness P* in union_{k in S} E_k(Z) maximizing h_hat and the maximizer of R, with recomputable values.
